documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.summary: The Provost page gives general guidelines for generative AI use (accuracy, confidential data, phishing, procurement), definitions, and FAQs for faculty, staff and students. It sets no AI rule for coursework: students are told to follow each instructor's policy and ask when unsure, and faculty are told to state expectations in the syllabus.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no stance of its own: students are told "Different fields, courses, and instructors will have different policies and guidelines for how AI can or cannot be used", and faculty are told to "be clear about expectations for student use of AI". The decision is handed to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: Opening framing sentence: "potential to facilitate research, revolutionize teaching" names benefits of generative AI without setting a rule, so it is a benefits statement (P87), informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI has the potential to facilitate research, revolutionize teaching

units.why: The page lists open concerns, "ethics and bias, business processes and efficiencies", as impacts of AI; it states worries, not a rule, so informs. P53 fits best because it names ethics and bias, but it also names learning and workforce, which P53 does not capture.
units.anchor: raising questions about student learning and assessment, ethics and bias
units.fit_note: Also names student learning, assessment, workforce and new opportunities, not only ethics and bias.

units.why: "It is your responsibility to ensure the accuracy of what is reported in your work" follows a warning that AI output "can include factual errors", so verification (P31) is a better type than P29.
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to ensure the accuracy of what is reported in your work.

units.why: "Review all material produced for accuracy, violations of copyright protections, and plagiarism" directs users to check AI output for copyright and plagiarism problems; P120 (unintentional plagiarism) fits best.
units.anchor: Review all material produced for accuracy, violations of copyright protections, and plagiarism.
units.fit_note: Also covers accuracy review and copyright, not only unintentional plagiarism.

units.why: "Document and be transparent about all uses of Generative AI" is a disclosure duty for every use, so P24 with must.
units.anchor: Document and be transparent about all uses of Generative AI

units.why: "Be sure to comply with academic and research integrity policies: review the Code of Student Life and Faculty Handbook" points users to existing policies they must follow, which is P77.
units.anchor: Be sure to comply with academic and research integrity policies

units.why: "In the classroom, be clear about expectations for student use of AI in their coursework" asks instructors to state their AI expectations; it does not name the syllabus, so P09 with a fit note.
units.anchor: be clear about expectations for student use of AI in their coursework
units.fit_note: Asks instructors to be clear about expectations but does not name the syllabus as the place.

units.why: "Data classified as private or restricted should not be entered into generative AI tools" is a data-protection rule citing SBHE 1202.3, so P50; unit stance restrict because it bars a type of input.
units.anchor: Data classified as private or restricted should not be entered into generative AI

units.why: "Do not disclose intellectual property that is not safeguarded" is about IP leaking into AI tools; it is an IP rule (P52) rather than the personal-data rule in the previous sentence.
units.anchor: Do not disclose intellectual property that is not safeguarded.
units.fit_note: Concerns not disclosing unsafeguarded IP to AI tools, not copyright or licensing of AI output.

units.why: "Be extra vigilant about potential phishing attacks. Generative AI is rapidly changing the phishing landscape" is AI-enabled phishing awareness, so P75.
units.anchor: Be extra vigilant about potential phishing attacks.

units.why: "Report any questionable emails to University Information Technology (UIT)" gives a channel for suspicious messages. P75 covers phishing reporting, nearest type; it is a separate action from staying vigilant.
units.anchor: Report any questionable emails to University Information Technology (UIT)

units.why: "submit procurement requests via Jaggaer regardless of the dollar value" requires institutional review before buying an AI tool, so P65 (broadened to approval before purchase).
units.anchor: submit procurement requests via Jaggaer regardless of the dollar value

units.why: "we expect these existing policies and guidelines to be modified or new policies to be created" says the guidance is provisional, which is P54.
units.anchor: we expect these existing policies and guidelines to be modified

units.anchor: computer systems that mimic or exceed human thinking based on experience
units.frag_end: identify patterns for predictions or decision-making.

units.why: "Generative AI is a form of AI used to create new content, images, text, videos, music" defines generative AI, so P61.

units.why: "it is important to understand your responsibilities and the related guidelines for ethical use" is a general call for responsible use with no specific content, so P116.
units.anchor: it is important to understand your responsibilities and the related guidelines for ethical use
